items.title: Activation of Amino Acids and the Phases of Translation

source_refs.note: Activation of amino acids and the three phases of translation (PDF 137-140), as printed; Figures 19.17 to 19.20 are replaced by original diagrams.

blocks.text: Before protein synthesis, the assemblage units are prepared. Specific tRNAs attach with specific amino acids and make aminoacyl-tRNAs (aa-tRNA). The enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase carries out this reaction. There are 20 kinds of this enzyme. Each kind binds to a specific amino acid. It also recognizes and binds to the tRNA with anticodons for that amino acid. The aa-tRNA delivers the amino acid to the ribosome for incorporation into the polypeptide chain.

blocks.alt: Left: a large green enzyme, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, holding an amino acid in one pocket and a tRNA in another, with the tRNA's anticodon end inside the enzyme. An arrow leads to the released aminoacyl-tRNA, the amino acid joined to the top of the tRNA, ready to participate in protein synthesis.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.17: Activation of amino acids (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.17).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Amino acid, tRNA, Anticodon, Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, Aminoacyl-tRNA, Ready to participate in protein synthesis.

blocks.text: In this phase, an initiation complex is formed in the following steps:

items: The aa-tRNA carrying the first amino acid binds to the smaller ribosomal subunit. An enzyme called initiation factor controls this binding. In prokaryotes, the first amino acid is modified methionine i.e., N-formyl-methionine. While in eukaryotes, it is non-modified methionine
Another initiation factor attaches the 5′ end of mRNA with smaller ribosomal subunit. It positions the anticodon of aa-tRNA over the first codon (AUG) of mRNA.
The larger ribosomal subunit is also placed upon smaller subunit.

blocks.text: The initiation complex formed in this way consists of both ribosomal subunits, first aa-tRNA, mRNA, and the enzyme.
The site of ribosome where first aa-tRNA is placed consists of;

items: A Peptidyl site (P site) – where peptide bonds will form between amino acids.
An aminoacyl site (A site) – where next aa-tRNA will bind.
An exit site (E site) – where empty tRNAs will exit the ribosome.

blocks.text: With respect to mRNA, the three sites are oriented in 5′ to 3′ as E-P-A, because ribosomes move toward the 3′ end of mRNA.

blocks.alt: Left: the smaller ribosomal subunit with mRNA and the aminoacyl-tRNA carrying Met, its anticodon UAC paired with the start codon AUG. A green arrow leads to the initiation complex: the larger subunit added, with the Met-tRNA in the P site between an empty E site and an empty A site.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.18: Initiation phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.18).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Aminoacyl tRNA, Smaller subunit, mRNA, Larger subunit, E site, P site, A site, Initiation complex, Met, UAC, AUG, 5', 3'.

blocks.text: In the initiation complex, the P-site of ribosome is occupied by first aa-tRNA (with its anticodon matching the mRNA codon). The next codon of mRNA is exposed at A site. Elongation happens in the following steps;

items: The next aa-tRNA with matching anticodon and matching amino acid binds to A site with the help of an enzyme, the elongation factor.
Another enzyme peptidyl transferase removes methionine from first aa-tRNA present on P site and attaches it by a peptide bond to the amino acid of the second aa-tRNA present at A site.
The ribosome moves three nucleotides along the mRNA in 5′ - 3′ direction. This movement is called translocation.

As a result of the previous step, the aa-tRNA carrying the chain of two amino acids is shifted from A site to P site. The new codon of mRNA is also exposed at A site. Moreover, the empty tRNA comes to E site to leave the ribosome.
These steps are repeated again and again until the stop codon is reached at A site.

blocks.alt: Seven numbered steps round a cycle on the mRNA AUG CUG UCU: (1) the Leu-tRNA (anticodon GAC) enters the A site next to the Met-tRNA in the P site; (2) Met is transferred to Leu, forming a peptide bond; (3) the ribosome moves one codon, the empty tRNA moves to the E site and leaves while the Ser-tRNA (anticodon AGA) arrives; (4) Ser-tRNA binds the A site; (5) the Met-Leu chain is transferred to Ser; (6) the ribosome moves on and the empty tRNA leaves; (7) the process repeats for all codons.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.19: Elongation phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.19).
blocks.long_description: The printed caption explains the frames: 1- second aminoacyl-tRNA binds to A site; 2- first amino acid is removed from first tRNA and attached to the amino acid of the second aminoacyl-tRNA; 3- ribosome moves three nucleotides in 5′ - 3′ direction; 4- third aminoacyl-tRNA binds to A site; 5- chain of first two amino acids is removed from the tRNA at P-site and attached to the amino acid of the third aminoacyl-tRNA; 6- ribosome again moves three nucleotides and next codon of mRNA is exposed at A site; 7- the process is repeated for all codons. Each frame shows the larger and smaller subunits, the E, P and A sites, the tRNAs with their anticodons UAC, GAC, AGA and the growing chain Met, Leu, Ser.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 19.19 shows the third codon as AAU in its first three frames and UCU later. The serine tRNA's anticodon AGA pairs only with UCU (AAU codes for asparagine), so the codon is UCU throughout, as drawn above.

When a stop codon is exposed at A site, no aminoacyl-tRNA comes to A-site (because there is no anticodon of the stop codons). Stop codon at A site is recognized by a protein called release factor. It releases the polypeptide from the tRNA present at P site. In this way, the process of translation is terminated. The tRNA is also released from ribosome and ribosomal subunits separate from the mRNA.

blocks.alt: Left: the ribosome with a tRNA (anticodon ACC) on UGG in the P site carrying the chain Met-Leu-Ser-Trp and the stop codon UAA in the A site; a release factor approaches. Middle: the release factor sits in the A site and the polypeptide is freed from the tRNA. Below: the polypeptide, the larger subunit, the smaller subunit, the tRNA and the release factor separate from the mRNA.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.20: Termination phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.20).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Release factor, Stop codon, Polypeptide, Larger subunit, Smaller subunit, tRNA, mRNA, E site, A site, 5', 3'.
